title: Pulse synchronizer

sources.document: TI The TTL Data Book for Design Engineers, 2nd ed. (1976), section 7, TYPES SN54120, SN74120 Dual pulse synchronizers/drivers, bulletin DL-S 7211537 (revised December 1972)

pins.name: 1M
pins.text: mode control: low passes a train of pulses, high passes a single pulse. Internal pull-up.

pins.name: 1S1
pins.text: start/stop latch input (see function table). Internal pull-up.

pins.name: 1S2
pins.text: start/stop latch input (see function table). Internal pull-up.

pins.name: 1R
pins.text: latch input; a high-to-low transition stops output pulses. Internal pull-up.

pins.name: 1C
pins.text: clock input whose pulses are passed to the outputs; no pull-up

functions.text: While the section is passing pulses, Y carries the clock pulses of C (16 ns typical from C); the start/stop latch and the clock latch decide whether a pulse is passed, and a pulse once started is passed in full (latched, not clipped). Formula is the behaviour described in the text, not the gate-level wiring.
Complement of Y (9 ns typical from C).

state.changesOn: levels and high-to-low transitions on R, S1, S2; clock C
rules: R X, S1 L, S2 X: pass output pulses
R X, S1 X, S2 L: pass output pulses
R L, S1 H, S2 H: inhibit output pulses
R H, S1 high-to-low, S2 H: start output pulses
R H, S1 H, S2 high-to-low: start output pulses
R high-to-low, S1 H, S2 H: stop output pulses
R H, S1 H, S2 H: continue (operation started by the last high-to-low transition continues)
After start, M low: pulses keep passing until a stop command; M high: only a single clock pulse is passed

When stopped by S or R, the setup times decide which is the last pulse. A low-to-high transition on M meeting tsu(H) passes that positive clock pulse, then inhibits remaining pulses. Low-to-high transitions on M in the 20 ns after the falling edge of the clock pulse may or may not let the next pulse through.
Once an output pulse has started it is not cut short (C is latch-controlled)

electrical.notes: Clock driver: outputs drive 60 Series 54/74 loads high and 30 loads low. M, R and S inputs have internal pull-up resistors (15 kOhm nominal shown in the input schematic) and may be left open; the C input has none. C input low-level current -3.2 mA max, other inputs -2.1 mA max.

stored.name: RUN1
stored.source: 7-118 (PDF page 117) - TI The TTL Data Book, 2nd ed. 1976, function table and description: S1 or S2 low passes pulses (and wins over R); R low with both S high inhibits; the last high-to-low transition continues. The datasheet has no gate diagram ("logic: see description and function table"); these bits are the behaviour of the function table and Figures 2-5, not the chip's gates.

stored.name: ST1
stored.source: 7-118 (PDF page 117) - TI The TTL Data Book, 2nd ed. 1976, function table and description, 7-122 (PDF page 121), Figures 4 and 5: a high-to-low transition on S1 or S2 is a new start; it flips this bit so a single pulse is allowed again. The datasheet has no gate diagram ("logic: see description and function table"); these bits are the behaviour of the function table and Figures 2-5, not the chip's gates.

stored.name: SEEN1
stored.next: SEEN1 = (EN1 AND 1M AND ST1) OR (NOT(EN1 AND 1M) AND SEEN1)
stored.source: 7-122 (PDF page 121), Figures 4 and 5: with M high only one clock pulse is passed after a start; at the end of a passed pulse with M high this bit catches up with ST, which stops further pulses. The datasheet has no gate diagram ("logic: see description and function table"); these bits are the behaviour of the function table and Figures 2-5, not the chip's gates.

stored.name: EN1
stored.next: EN1 = PASS1 AND (NOT 1M OR (ST1 XOR SEEN1))
stored.source: 7-118 (PDF page 117) - TI The TTL Data Book, 2nd ed. 1976, function table and description: C is latch-controlled, an output pulse once started is passed in full; 7-121 (PDF page 120), Figures 2 and 3: setup times are measured to the rising edge of the clock, where this latch closes. The datasheet has no gate diagram ("logic: see description and function table"); these bits are the behaviour of the function table and Figures 2-5, not the chip's gates.
